ai.name: AI
ai.def: Artificial intelligence: computer systems that do tasks which normally need human thinking.

model.name: Model
model.def: The saved pattern an AI has learned. You give it input and it gives back an answer.

training.name: Training
training.def: The slow step where an AI studies many examples and learns the pattern.

inference.name: Inference
inference.def: Using a trained model on new input to get an answer. This step is fast.

hallucination.name: Hallucination
hallucination.def: When an AI gives an answer that sounds sure but is wrong or made up.

machine-learning.name: Machine learning
machine-learning.def: A way to build AI where the computer learns from examples instead of fixed rules.

neural-network.name: Neural network
neural-network.def: A model made of many simple connected units in layers. It is loosely inspired by the brain.

llm.name: LLM
llm.def: Large language model: a deep learning model trained on huge amounts of text, used by chatbots.

generative-ai.name: Generative AI
generative-ai.def: AI that creates new content, such as text, pictures, sound or code.

prompt.name: Prompt
prompt.def: The question or instruction you give to an AI.

token.name: Token
token.def: A small piece of text, like a word or part of a word, that an LLM reads and writes.

data-science.name: Data science
data-science.def: Using data, statistics and often machine learning to find answers and make predictions.

data-analytics.name: Data analytics
data-analytics.def: Looking at data to answer questions about what happened and why. Often done with tables and charts.

data-engineering.name: Data engineering
data-engineering.def: Building the systems that collect, move, store and clean data so others can use it.

pipeline.name: Pipeline
pipeline.def: A series of steps that moves data from where it starts to where it is used.

synthetic-data.name: Synthetic data
synthetic-data.def: Made-up data created for learning or testing. It is not real measurements.

lessons.title: What is AI?

cards.title: AI in one sentence
lines: AI is a computer that learns from examples.
It does not only follow rules a person wrote.
It finds patterns, then uses them on new cases.

cards.title: Rulebook or apprentice?
lines: A protection relay follows a rulebook.
If current is too high for too long, it trips.
Every rule was written by a person.
An apprentice learns differently. He watches thousands of past jobs and starts to see what usually happens.
AI is like that apprentice.

cards.title: Two ways to spot a fault
lines: Rule way: set a pickup, compare the current, trip.
Learning way: show the model 1,000 recorded faults, each with a label.
It learns what a real fault looks like.
Then it can flag a new record that looks odd, for a person to review.

cards.title: Training and using
lines: Training: the model studies many examples. This is slow.
Inference: the model answers a new question. This is fast.
When you chat with an AI assistant, you are doing inference.

cards.title: AI can be wrong
lines: AI guesses the most likely answer.
It can sound sure and still be wrong.
So we always check important answers.

cards.title: A rule for every engineer
lines: AI must never change protection settings by itself.
A qualified engineer checks every setting.
Use approved procedures, the maker's manual and the standards.
This site is for learning. It is not engineering advice.

cards.title: AI is already around you
lines: Email spam filter: learns from messages people marked as spam.
Voice typing: turns your speech into text.
Map apps: guess travel time from past traffic.

cards.title: Practice: rule or pattern?
lines: Write down 3 tasks from your work.
Mark each one RULE (fixed steps) or PATTERN (needs experience).
Example of a rule: check the CT ratio against the drawing.
Example of a pattern: notice that a test result looks odd.

cards.title: Recap
lines: AI learns patterns from examples.
A relay follows rules. AI learns from data.
AI can be wrong, so engineers check it.

quiz.q: A relay trips when current is above its setting. Is this AI?
options: No, it follows a fixed rule
quiz.why: The relay applies a rule written by a person. AI learns patterns from examples.

quiz.q: What is 'inference'?
options: Using a trained model on new input
quiz.why: Training teaches the model. Inference is using it afterwards.

quiz.q: Which is the best description of AI today?
options: Software that learns patterns from data
A list of fixed if-then rules
quiz.why: Most useful AI is software that learns patterns from examples.

quiz.q: An AI gives a confident answer. What should you do for an important result?
options: Check it with a reliable source
quiz.why: AI can be wrong while sounding sure. Always verify important answers.

quiz.q: Who must approve protection settings?
options: A qualified engineer using approved procedures
quiz.why: AI may assist, but a qualified engineer decides, using manuals, procedures and standards.

lessons.career: AI is most useful to a relay engineer as an assistant: summarising manuals, drafting test reports and flagging unusual results. You stay responsible for every decision.

lessons.title: AI, Machine Learning and Deep Learning

cards.title: Three words, one family
lines: AI is the big idea.
Machine learning is one way to do AI.
Deep learning is one kind of machine learning.
Everything in the small circle is also in the bigger ones.

cards.title: Boxes inside boxes
lines: Open the biggest box. It says AI.
Inside is a smaller box: machine learning.
Inside that is the smallest box: deep learning.

cards.title: Machine learning
lines: You give the computer examples.
It finds the pattern by itself.
It works well on tables of numbers.
It often needs less data than deep learning.

cards.title: Deep learning
lines: It uses a neural network with many layers.
Early layers find simple things. Later layers find bigger things.
It is great for photos, sound and text.
It needs lots of data and computing power.

cards.title: Example: a table of numbers
lines: Predict transformer risk from oil gas readings, load and temperature.
The inputs are numbers in columns.
This is classic machine learning.

cards.title: Example: a picture
lines: Read a relay nameplate from a photo.
Check a panel photo for loose or missing parts.
Pictures usually need deep learning.

cards.title: A risk score is a helper
lines: A risk score helps plan maintenance.
It does not replace inspection or testing.
An engineer makes the final decision.

cards.title: Practice: sort these
lines: Is each one AI only, machine learning, or deep learning?
1. Alarm filter written as if-then rules.
2. Model that predicts oil temperature from past load numbers.
3. Software that reads a meter display from a photo.
4. Chatbot that summarises a manual.
Answers: 1 AI only, 2 machine learning, 3 deep learning, 4 deep learning.

cards.title: Recap
lines: AI is the big idea. ML learns from data.
Deep learning is ML with many layers.
Pick the simplest tool that works.

quiz.q: Which circle is the biggest?
quiz.why: AI is the widest idea. ML is inside AI, and deep learning is inside ML.

quiz.q: Deep learning is built on...
quiz.why: Deep learning uses neural networks with many layers.

quiz.q: Which task most likely needs deep learning?
options: Reading a nameplate from a photo
Sorting a list A to Z
quiz.why: Pictures, sound and language are where deep learning is strongest.

quiz.q: For a small table of numbers, which is often a good first choice?
quiz.why: Simple ML often works well on tables and needs less data.

quiz.q: A transformer risk score should be used to...
quiz.why: A risk score supports planning. Inspection, testing and engineers still decide.

lessons.career: When you read a job advert or a tool's website, these three words help you see what is really offered and which skills to learn first.

lessons.title: Generative AI and Large Language Models

cards.title: Generative AI makes new things
lines: Many AI tools sort or predict.
Generative AI creates: text, pictures, sound and code.
Chatbots and image tools are examples.

cards.title: What is an LLM?
lines: LLM means large language model.
It is trained on a huge amount of text.
It learns which words usually follow other words.
Then it writes new text one small piece at a time.

cards.title: Autocomplete, but much bigger
lines: Your phone suggests the next word as you type.
An LLM does the same, with far more reading behind it.
That is why it sounds fluent.
It does not know things the way a person does.

cards.title: Prompts
lines: You give an LLM a prompt: your question or instruction.
A clear prompt gives a better answer.
We practise this in Module 2.

cards.title: What it can do for a relay engineer
lines: Summarise a long relay manual.
Draft a test checklist.
Explain a protection term in simple words.
Turn rough notes into a neat report.

cards.title: What it cannot do
lines: It can make up facts. This is called a hallucination.
It cannot see your relay or your test set.
It may not know a new firmware or a rare relay model.
It can get numbers wrong.

cards.title: Protect confidential data
lines: Do not paste company documents or customer data into public AI tools without permission.
Check every number, setting and limit against the maker's manual.
AI output is a draft. It is not an approved procedure.

cards.title: Practice: test an AI
lines: Open a free AI assistant on your phone.
Ask it to explain overcurrent protection in 5 simple lines.
Check the answer against a trusted textbook or manual.
Write one thing it got right and one thing you had to verify.

cards.title: Recap
lines: Generative AI creates new content.
An LLM predicts text, so it can sound right and be wrong.
Use it as a helper. Verify and protect confidential data.

quiz.q: What does an LLM mainly do?
quiz.why: It is trained on text and writes new text piece by piece.

quiz.q: What is a hallucination?
options: A confident answer that is wrong or made up
quiz.why: Hallucinations sound sure but are false or invented.

quiz.q: What is a prompt?
options: Your question or instruction to the AI
quiz.why: The prompt is what you type to the AI.

quiz.q: Which is safe to paste into a public AI tool?
options: A general question about how overcurrent protection works
quiz.why: General learning questions are fine. Never share confidential data without permission.

quiz.q: An AI gives a pickup value for a relay. What do you do?
options: Check it against the manual and approved settings
quiz.why: Numbers must be verified against manufacturer documents and approved procedures.

lessons.career: LLMs are the tool most engineers will meet first. Using them well and safely is a real workplace skill.

lessons.title: Data Science, Analytics and Data Engineering

cards.title: Data is the fuel
lines: AI and machine learning need data.
Data science is the work of getting answers from data.
It has three main parts, and each is a different job.

cards.title: Three jobs with data
lines: Data engineering: collect, move and clean the data.
Data analytics: look at the data and answer questions.
Data science: build models that predict what may happen next.

cards.title: A water supply
lines: The data engineer builds the pipes and tanks.
The data analyst tests the water and reports what is in it.
The data scientist predicts how much water we need next month.

cards.title: Example: relay test data
lines: Engineer: gather test results from many relays into one clean table.
Analyst: chart operating time against the allowed limit.
Scientist: predict which relay may drift out of tolerance.
These are educational examples, not real procedures.

cards.title: Analytics or science?
lines: Analytics asks: what happened, and why?
Data science asks: what will probably happen next?
Both start with clean data.

cards.title: Why clean data matters
lines: Wrong units, missing values and typing mistakes give wrong answers.
Example: mixing milliseconds with seconds.
Clean first. Analyse second.

cards.title: Real limits come from real documents
lines: Data in this course is made up, called synthetic data.
Real acceptance limits come from the manufacturer's documents and your approved test procedure.

cards.title: Practice: spot the data
lines: List 5 things on a relay test sheet. Use names only, no real values.
Example: pickup current, operating time, tolerance, pass or fail, date.
Mark each as a number or a label.

cards.title: Recap
lines: Engineering moves data. Analytics explains it. Science predicts.
Clean data comes first.
Use made-up data for learning. Use approved documents for real limits.

quiz.q: Who builds the systems that collect and clean data?
quiz.why: Data engineers build the pipelines and storage.

quiz.q: Which question is data analytics?
options: What happened last month, and why?
How do I build a neural network?
quiz.why: Analytics explains what already happened.

quiz.q: Which job usually builds prediction models?
quiz.why: Data scientists build and test predictive models.

quiz.q: Why is clean data important?
options: Wrong or mixed data gives wrong answers
It is a rule from AI
quiz.why: Bad inputs give bad results, for example mixing seconds and milliseconds.

quiz.q: Where do real acceptance limits come from?
options: Manufacturer documents and approved test procedures
quiz.why: Learning data is synthetic. Real limits come from approved documents.

lessons.career: Most electrical engineers start with data analytics. It uses the test and log data you already produce.

lessons.title: How AI, ML, Deep Learning and Data Science Fit Together

cards.title: One family, different jobs
lines: AI, machine learning and deep learning are nested.
Data science overlaps with machine learning. It also uses statistics and charts.
Think of them as tools in one workshop.

cards.title: Side by side
lines: Slide the table sideways on a small screen.
Use it to compare the four ideas quickly.

head: Topic
AI
Machine learning
Deep learning
Data science
rows: Needs lots of data and power

cards.title: What they share
lines: All of them use data.
All of them can be wrong.
All of them need a person to check the result.

cards.title: Use cases for your field
lines: Rules: simple alarms and checks.
Machine learning: predict equipment condition.
Deep learning: read photos and documents.
Data science: find patterns in test and event data.

cards.title: Limits to remember
lines: Bad data gives bad answers.
Models can be biased if the data is one-sided.
A model that works on test data may fail on real plants.
None of these replaces engineering judgement.

cards.title: Careers (no promises)
lines: Roles change often, so these are examples only.
The table shows what each role mainly does.

head: Role
Mainly does
Good first skill
rows: Uses AI tools in protection, testing and service

cards.title: Practice: pick the tool
lines: For each task, name the best fit: rules, machine learning, deep learning or data analytics.
1. Flag a relay when current is above a set limit.
2. Read a meter display from a photo.
3. Chart this year's operating times in a table.
4. Predict which breaker may fail from past records.
Answers: 1 rules, 2 deep learning, 3 data analytics, 4 machine learning.

cards.title: Recap
lines: AI is the big idea. ML and DL sit inside it.
Data science overlaps and relies on clean data.
Choose the simplest tool that solves the problem.

quiz.q: Which statement is correct?
options: Deep learning is inside machine learning
Data science is a type of deep learning
quiz.why: Deep learning is a part of machine learning, which is a part of AI.

quiz.q: Which tool fits 'chart operating times'?
quiz.why: Charting existing numbers is analytics.

quiz.q: What do all four fields have in common?
options: They use data and need checking
quiz.why: Data in, results out, and a person verifies.

quiz.q: Which is a real limit of ML models?
options: They always work on every plant
Poor or biased data gives poor results
quiz.why: Data quality decides model quality.

quiz.q: Which is the best first move for a beginner engineer?
options: Learn to use AI tools and analyse data
quiz.why: AI use and data analysis come first. ML comes later.

lessons.career: Knowing what each field does helps you choose which skill to learn next and understand what job adverts really ask for.

lessons.title: Your Skills and Your Path

cards.title: Why AI comes first
lines: You can use AI today with no coding.
It helps your daily work: reading, writing and checking.
You learn how to use it safely.

cards.title: Why data analysis is next
lines: Your work already makes data: test results, readings and logs.
A spreadsheet can already analyse it.
It builds the skills that machine learning needs later.

cards.title: Why machine learning comes later
lines: ML needs clean data, some maths ideas and some coding.
Without them, models are easy to get wrong.
So ML follows data analysis and Python.

cards.title: Skills that help electrical engineers
lines: Open the table to see skill, reason and when to learn it.

cards.title: Your edge is your field
lines: Many people can write code.
Few understand why a relay trips.
AI plus protection knowledge is your edge.

cards.title: Your road map
lines: 1. AI fundamentals.
2. AI power user.
3. Excel and data analysis.
4. Python.
5. Statistics.
6. Machine learning.
7. Applied AI projects.
8. Electrical specialisation.
9. Advanced AI.

cards.title: Practice: make your plan
lines: Write which step you are on today.
Pick one small thing to do this week.
Write one question you want answered.

cards.title: Recap
lines: Start with AI use. Then data analysis. Then Python and ML.
Your protection knowledge is your edge.
You may revisit any lesson at any time.

quiz.q: Why does data analysis come before machine learning?
options: It builds skills ML needs, and uses data you already have
quiz.why: Data analysis builds data skills and gives value early.

quiz.q: Which skill can you start now with no laptop?
quiz.why: Using AI tools safely works on a phone.

quiz.q: What is your main edge as an electrical engineer?
options: Knowing the domain, such as protection
quiz.why: Domain knowledge tells you what the data means.

quiz.q: When is Python best learned?
options: When you have a laptop for practice
quiz.why: Python is best practised on a computer.

quiz.q: Do you have to follow the order strictly?
options: No, you can revisit topics and skip what you do not need
Only if the AI says so
quiz.why: The order is a guide. Revisit any lesson when you need it.

lessons.career: A clear plan beats random learning. Come back to this lesson whenever you feel lost.
